expected_level_description: You can: - clearly explain problems and design ideas to others - clearly explain design decisions to others using appropriate tools and methods

You can: - design and deliver inclusive, accessible and environmentally sustainable content or services that meet the needs of all users, working with others - ensure your design work meets appropriate standards and guidance, for example accessibility regulations, with support

You can: - align your design work to both the goals and vision of your team and the strategic objectives of your organisation - identify potential risks and use design to mitigate them - identify opportunities and use design to take advantage of them - contribute to the development of design patterns and components

You can: - effectively plan and run a design session with your team, users or stakeholders - identify and engage the right people throughout the design process - give and receive constructive design feedback

You can: - work with researchers and analysts to draw together, analyse and clearly explain commonly available evidence relevant to users or a service, for example, web analytics data - use evidence to inform, develop and test a design idea, with support

You can: - apply iterative design principles and techniques and agile methodologies to your work - create material to test ideas and hypotheses at an appropriate fidelity, for example mockups or drafts - iterate and improve a design based on successive rounds of research - use and iterate design patterns and components

You can: - lead and coordinate design work in your team, with support - communicate the value of user-centred design to your team or others in your organisation - support other designers - work with digital and data leaders in your organisation, when needed

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it

skill: Designing for clinical safety and human factors
expected_level_description: You can: - design interfaces that make the safe action the easy action, for example by reducing ambiguous labels and needless alerts - test designs in realistic clinical scenarios, including interruptions and time pressure - raise design-related hazards with the clinical safety officer and record how designs control them
You can: - recognise and challenge behaviour that excludes others - consider different needs when you plan your work
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
